title: How a Lock and Key Works in 60 Seconds 🔑🔒 #shorts
description:
The pin tumbler lock is an idea about 4,000 years old, from ancient Egypt, and Linus Yale Jr. turned it into the compact cylinder lock in the 1860s. Inside, spring-loaded pin stacks block a rotating plug. The bumps on the right key lift every pin to exactly the shear line, so the plug can turn. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#lock #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The lock on your door uses an idea about *4,000 years* old, first seen in ancient Egypt.

steps.label: Plug
steps.text: Inside is a *plug* that wants to turn, sitting in a fixed outer *housing*.

steps.label: Pins
steps.text: Stacks of *pins* cross the gap. Springs push them down, so the plug is jammed.

steps.label: Key
steps.text: Slide in the right key, and each bump lifts its pin to a *different height*.

steps.label: Shear line
steps.text: Now every gap between pins lines up exactly with the *shear line*.

steps.label: Turn
steps.text: Nothing blocks the plug anymore, so it *turns* and pulls the bolt back.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pins, key, *shear line*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
